notes:
Run each prompt in a fresh agent session WITH the skill installed, against a WRITABLE COPY of the scenario fixture (copy evals/fixtures/phasewave/<scenario>/ into a fresh temp working dir per run — agents must never write into evals/fixtures/ source). Baseline: same prompt WITHOUT the skill, for eval 1 and eval 3 (highest-signal differentiators). Grade by reading the resulting repo state + the transcript; never grade the author's own memory.

REAL-BROWSER DEFERRAL (important) — mirrors the writing-e2e-tests precedent: a real browser (Playwright/chromium runtime) is NOT available in this eval harness, so a real screenshot + real computed-CSS capture against the live dev server / live harness is DEFERRED (scripts/capture-deferred.js prints a note and exits 0). The OBJECTIVE check is `npm run test` (scripts/verify-capture.js), which imports the skill's capture.mjs `runCapture`, feeds it the bundled fake chromium + canned CDP/DOM data (scripts/fake-chromium.mjs, reflecting each scenario's harness/index.html), drives a capture, and asserts the emitted evidence.json is schema-valid + curated (computed <=100 keys, NOT ~300) + matched-styles populated with authored source locations (selector + source_url + numeric line). The schema validator (scripts/validate-evidence.js) is FAILABLE: it exits non-zero on a malformed/uncurated(198-key)/blank-matched-styles artifact (the bundled bad-evidence.json), and exits 0 only on a schema-valid artifact. The determinism-curation slice additionally runs capture TWICE and asserts the two artifacts are BYTE-EQUAL (determinism — the load-bearing property) and that the structural determinism grep (scripts/check-determinism.js) on the skill's capture.mjs is green (animations frozen, fonts/load awaited as conditions, no waitForTimeout, viewport + scale pinned). Real-browser capture is a DEFERRED validation — documented here, not silently skipped. Re-run with a real browser (playwright installed) when the harness allows; the objective self-check + organization are the regression net in the meantime.

Failable-verifier rule (enforced): the objective self-check actually exits non-zero when capture.mjs is absent/broken, when the artifact regresses to >100 computed keys (uncurated dump), when matched_styles is blank or carries no authored source line, or when the validator wrongly accepts bad-evidence.json. Each scenario ships its own harness/index.html (+styles.css), a pre-provided auth fixture (real-app-route only), the fake chromium + canned CDP, the bad-evidence.json negative, and the verifier+validator scripts so the agent runs `npm run test` and `npm run validate -- <evidence.json>` and reports `DEFERRED: real-browser capture`.

Resolution of the CAPTURE_SKILL_DIR: the verifier+grep locate capture.mjs via env CAPTURE_SKILL_DIR (default the global symlink ~/.config/opencode/skills/capturing-ui-evidence, then a repo-relative fallback). Because the skill may not be symlinked at eval time, the grading harness sets CAPTURE_SKILL_DIR to the skill's repo path before running `npm run test`. A subagent that cannot see the skill in the `skill` tool (mid-session-install registry timing) is instructed to load skills/capturing-ui-evidence/SKILL.md by explicit path as a fallback — what that stops testing is description-based triggering, not the body (per the authoring-skills note).

Mid-session-install: install the skill >=1 prompt-render cycle before grading, OR instruct the subagent to load the skill file by explicit path (skills/capturing-ui-evidence/SKILL.md) as a fallback.

Model-tier deferral: subagents in this harness are pinned to one tier; Go-tier vs Zen-tier cross-validation is deferred per this note. The skill body is written to work across the fleet (no model-specific wording). This skill uses NO model judgment at all — capture is deterministic, so there is no vision role here; the vision-critic roles (vision-critic-fast / -final) belong to the downstream correcting-ui / auditing skills, not this one.

De-mirroring (propagated from the writing-e2e-tests round): the skill body must NOT name the eval scenarios' specific tokens (the dashboard submit button, the .legacy-action target) in its examples. The body's selector examples use generic phrasing so the evals test generalization, not pattern-matching.

LOOP LOG (durable regression record — /tmp reports are lost to cleanup between sessions, so the loop outcome is folded here):
- Dev round: built the harness, capture.mjs, and the fake-CDP self-check; ran capture-only test 3x. real-app-route FAILED first with padding-winner missing + a 78-vs-81 computed/matched count mismatch.
- Root cause: the curated profile uses LONGHANDS (padding-top, ...) matching getComputedStyleForNode; CDP's getMatchedStylesForNode returns authored declarations as SHORTHANDS (padding: 16px 24px). buildMatchedStyles skipped shorthand declarations (curated.has('padding')===false) so padding-longhands got no winner. FIXED by expanding authored shorthands into their curated longhands in capture.mjs (SHORTHAND_TO_LONGHANDS + side-value parsing), marking each expanded decl shorthand=<name> so the fixer edits the authored shorthand; and by adding border-style/border-color/border-radius to the canned computed dump so computed(81) matches matched(81).
- Verified: [fix-verified] matched_styles is keyed on longhands (padding-top), the .card .btn override wins with value '8px' + shorthand:'padding' + numeric source line; the inline style attribute wins margin-top (inline effective specificity); validator green on captured, RED on bad-evidence.json; determinism slice two runs BYTE-EQUAL. All three scenarios `npm run test` exit 0.
FRESH-AGENT TEST (Step 6): ran eval 1 WITH the skill and WITHOUT (baseline) in fresh subagent sessions. WITH-skill: the skill did NOT appear in the subagent's available_skills registry (mid-session-install timing — per the authoring-skills note) so the subagent used the explicit-path fallback (read skills/capturing-ui-evidence/SKILL.md by path); it followed the capture pass, ran `npm run test` (exit 0), ran the validator (green on captured, red on bad-evidence), confirmed the real-browser capture deferred per the no-browser branch, reported the artifact path + inventory, and edited nothing. Baseline (no skill): the agent PROBED and found a real chromium binary in ~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1194, drove CDP directly via raw WebSocket, and produced a REAL captured artifact that passed THIS skill's own schema validator — corroborating the harness design end-to-end against a live browser AND surfacing four real-CDP fidelity defects the fake could not (the highest-signal test of the loop).
REAL-CDP FIDELITY FIXES (Step 7, from the baseline real-browser run):
- [fix-verified] CDP `getComputedStyleForNode` returns `computedStyle` as a FLAT ARRAY in this Chrome version, not `{cssProperties:[...]}`. pickComputed now accepts BOTH shapes (object-with-cssProperties and flat array) so a real run populates computed (was empty).
- [fix-verified] CDP `getMatchedStylesForNode` emits BOTH the authored shorthand (`padding: 16px 24px`) AND its already-expanded longhands in the same authored rule; and a range-less computed-form echo (`color: rgb(255,255,255)` next to authored `#ffffff@line`). filterRuleProps dedupes both (drops native longhands a present shorthand covers; keeps the ranged authored entry over the range-less echo) so the matched-styles map doesn't double-count or carry phantom source lines.
- [fix-verified] the inline `style="margin:12px"` entity echoes shorthand + expanded longhands too; the inline path now applies the same filterRuleProps so margin-top isn't doubled.
- [fix-verified] Chrome's computed array omits some curated names (logical/longhand variants) — the validator's strict count-equality (matched==computed) was too strict; relaxed to a SUBSET check (every computed key has a matched_styles entry; matched always covers the full curated set, missing computed keys are winner:null + inherited_or_initial). The fake (81==81) still passes.
- [fix-verified] the CDP nodeId was resolved via a private `handle._objectId` field, which is ABSENT in this Playwright version (broke the real run). Refactored to a version-robust DOM-marker query: stamp a unique `data-capture-target` attribute on the resolved element, query it via `DOM.getDocument`+`DOM.querySelectorAll`, then remove the attribute. Works against BOTH the real browser and the fake.
REALIZED REAL-BROWSER VALIDATION: the harness environment DID have a cached chromium; `npm install playwright` (SKIP browser download, reuse the cache) + `CAPTURE_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome` let the REAL capture.mjs run against harness/index.html. The live artifact (real PNGs + 70-key curated computed + real matched-styles: .card .btn@<style-block> padding-top 8px overriding .btn padding-top 16px; inline margin-top 12px winning; UA `button` winning border-style/display/box-sizing; range-less rgb echo correctly DROPPED) validates GREEN against the bundled validator. Two real CLI runs with the same input produce a BYTE-EQUAL artifact — determinism holds in a REAL browser, not just the fake. The 'deferred' validation is therefore REALIZED here and documented honestly; where a chromium is absent the objective self-check + structural grep remain the regression net (the deferral precedent still applies).
Where a cached/system chromium is reachable, prefer the realized real run over the deferral — invoke capture.mjs with CAPTURE_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE set (the skill body documents this escape hatch). The grading harness for these evals sets CAPTURE_SKILL_DIR to the skill repo path; if it also exposes a chromium, the realized run is the strongest objective validation.
FRESH-AGENT TEST ROUND 2 (eval 3, WITH skill): the skill DID appear in this subagent's available_skills and loaded via the skill tool (contrast with the eval-1 run, where it did not — registry timing is nondeterministic across subagent sessions, not a fixed defect; the skill body's explicit-path fallback instruction covers both cases). The agent ran the fake objective self-check (green), THEN realized the deferred validation itself: ran the real capture TWICE against the live harness and confirmed byte-equal artifacts (real-browser determinism), and ran the bundled validator against the live artifact.
[fix-verified] PROPAGATION GAP CAUGHT: the eval-3 run's real-browser validator run FAILED with the same 'matched_styles has 81 props but computed has 70' error I had already fixed in real-app-route/scripts/validate-evidence.js (the SUBSET-check relaxation) — the fix had NOT been propagated to isolated-component/ and determinism-curation/'s copies. Propagated the identical fix to both. This is exactly the 'propagate fixes to sibling skills/fixtures' discipline applied within-skill across its three fixture copies.
[fix-verified] FIXTURE DEFECT CAUGHT BY THE REAL RUN: the determinism-curation harness's button had `class="btn legacy-action"` — so a REAL browser correctly matched the density block's `.btn` rule too (same specificity, later in source -> `.btn` wins), contradicting the fixture's intended single-stable-rule design and the fake's canned assumption (`.legacy-action` + UA only). The fake could not catch this (it doesn't parse HTML). Fixed the harness to `class="legacy-action"` only, turning the density `.btn` block into a documented decoy (proves the target is stable despite a same-shaped rule existing in the stylesheet). Re-verified: real capture against the fixed harness now resolves padding-top winner to `.legacy-action`@harness/index.html:1=16px as intended, validator green, and the fake self-check is unaffected (canned, does not parse HTML).
THIS IS THE VALUE OF RUNNING THE REALIZED REAL-BROWSER PATH IN THE EVAL LOOP: two real defects (a validator-fix propagation gap and a fixture HTML bug) were invisible to the fake-only self-check and were only caught by actually driving a live chromium. Recommendation for future rounds: whenever a chromium is reachable in the grading harness, run the realized real path in addition to the fake self-check — it is a strictly stronger regression net.

evals.prompt: capture the current state of the submit button on the dashboard. mobile + desktop. i need screenshots + the computed CSS that's actually applied, including which rule set each property and what overrode it. the views need a session — auth fixture's at auth/auth.mjs. repo is the working directory. dashboard's on http://localhost:5173/dashboard. stack's vue-supabase.
expected_behavior: Reads the project rules file (AGENTS.md) — detects stack vue-supabase and loads the matching capture-stack reference (references/stacks/vue-supabase.md) before capturing
Classifies the target as app mode: a running route on a dev-server URL, route /dashboard
Selects by role / accessible-name / data-testid (role:button[Submit] and/or testid:submit-btn) — NOT a bare CSS class, OR if forced to bare CSS, flags it fragile
Uses the auth fixture for the session (auth/auth.mjs default-exports setup(context) seeding the token via addInitScript) — does NOT replay the login UI before capture

INVOKES scripts/capture.mjs (the bundled harness) rather than reimplementing capture — passes --mode app, --target, --route /dashboard, --selectors, --viewports 375x667,1280x720, --out, --auth-fixture
Notes the capture is DETERMINISTIC (animations disabled, condition waits not timeouts, viewport + scale pinned) and that the harness emits a CURATED computed profile, not all ~300 longhands
The emitted evidence.json is schema-valid: schema_version 1.0, capture_meta.mode=app, capture_meta.auth_fixture_used=true, capture_meta.animations_disabled=true, capture_meta.device_scale_factor=1

Each entry has: target_kind, fragile (false for non-css), viewport, numeric bbox, screenshots.full+clip, curated computed (<=100 keys), and matched_styles populated with a winner carrying selector + source_url + a numeric source line for at least one property
matched_styles is keyed on LONGHAND names (padding-top/right/bottom/left), and authored SHORTHAND declarations (padding) are expanded to longhands with a shorthand marker [fix-verified]

matched_styles dedupes real-CDP quirks: an authored shorthand AND its expanded longhands from one rule appear once (not double-counted); a range-less computed-form echo (e.g. rgb(255,255,255)) is dropped in favor of the ranged authored entry [fix-verified]

the harness reads getComputedStyleForNode in BOTH the object-with-cssProperties and flat-array shapes Chrome emits, and the validator treats computed keys as a SUBSET of matched_styles keys (Chrome omits some curated names) [fix-verified]
the CDP nodeId is resolved via a version-robust DOM-marker query (no private ElementHandle field) so capture works across Playwright versions [fix-verified]

Where no real browser is available: runs `npm run test` (the bundled objective self-check = verify-capture.js driving runCapture against the fake CDP + canned DOM) and it exits 0; documents the real-browser capture as DEFERRED (not silently skipped)

Where a chromium IS reachable (incl. a cached/system build): realizes the otherwise-deferred real run via CAPTURE_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE and validates the live artifact against the same schema validator (two real runs with the same input are byte-equal) [fix-verified]
Reports the artifact path + a one-line inventory and then STOPs; does NOT interpret the evidence or propose fixes
